_doc: Layer inventory for the inversion atlas. Derived from the legacy state_io.js KNOWN_LAYERS table. Each layer declares its tier (hot/warm/cold), source (file/operation), pre-warm trigger, and optional chunking strategy for v2 large-track support. Path templating uses {slot} substitution from AtlasState.shared.* and resolve() args.
_v2_changes_2026-05-06: Three additions: (1) per-candidate paths now include {version_id} and resolve() throws if version_id is missing for those layers (no fallback default — versioning is mandatory); (2) candidate_lineage layer added — the version index for each candidate; (3) writable: true marks layers that Registry.write() may write to (per-candidate JSONs and lineage). Server-compute layers gain persist: true — every operation result is also written to the server results cache (configured at popstats_server.config.yaml > server_results_cache_root, default /mnt/e/inversion-atlas-cache/server_results/).

_tier_legend.hot: RAM-pinned at trigger event; pages read state directly; <1ms
_tier_legend.warm: IndexedDB-cached at trigger event; first read async ~50ms; subsequent ~10ms

layers._section_1: ==== HOT layers (pre-warmed to RAM at chrom_change) ====

scrubber_main._auto_index_doc: Filename per chrom is discovered at runtime via GET /api/precomp_index?root=precomp_zblocks. The server walks the root, returns {LG01: 'C_gar_LG01.atlas.json', ...} and the registry constructs <root_path>/<filename>. No need to hardcode the species prefix or the .atlas infix; the same layer keeps working when the pipeline's naming convention changes or when a second species lands.
scrubber_main._root_doc: Resolved through master_config.yaml -> roots.precomp_zblocks (currently /mnt/e/results_inversions/local_PCA_MDS_z/09_atlas_json/). To switch precomp source, edit the root entry — no layer change needed.
scrubber_main._worker_parse_doc: 2026-05-26: precomp scrubber JSONs run 20-60 MB per chrom; main-thread JSON.parse blocks paint/scroll for ~300-800 ms. atlas-core/core/worker_json_parse.js offloads to a Web Worker so the page stays interactive during mount. Wall-clock is roughly the same (structured-clone cost mirrors the parse) but the page no longer freezes.
scrubber_main._v2_chunked_plan: When whole-genome support arrives, set chunked: true and split <chrom>.json into <chrom>_<window_block>.json shards.

scrubber_thetapi._auto_index_doc: Same discovery mechanism as scrubber_main but pointed at the theta-pi pipeline root. Layout is nested (04_atlas_json/C_gar_LG{NN}/C_gar_LG{NN}_phase2_theta.json); the server's depth-2 scan handles it. Consumed by local_pca_theta_pi (local PCA θπ) via _buildLegacyState's merge of tracks_thetapi into state.data.
scrubber_thetapi._worker_parse_doc: Same shape + size class as scrubber_main; offloaded to the Web Worker so the local_pca_dosage mount's Promise.all([thetapi, ghsl]) doesn't pile two heavy parses onto the main thread back-to-back.

scrubber_ghsl._auto_index_doc: Same discovery mechanism as scrubber_main but pointed at the GHSL pipeline root. Pre-wired for symmetry with scrubber_thetapi; resolves to whatever filename convention the GHSL pipeline lands on, because the layer asks the server which files exist instead of templating.
scrubber_ghsl._worker_parse_doc: Same rationale as scrubber_main / scrubber_thetapi: heavy precomp JSON, parse blocks paint; worker keeps the main thread interactive.

repeat_density._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit repeat_density.scrubber_windows.json — flagged so prewarm + registry.resolve skip silently instead of spamming 404s. Remove when the pipeline produces the file.

band_nodes._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit band_nodes.tsv. Re-enable when the R band-tracking pipeline lands.

band_edges._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit band_edges.tsv. Re-enable when the R band-tracking pipeline lands.

transition_events._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit transition_events.tsv.

band_trajectories._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit band_trajectories.tsv.

het_band_backbones._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit het_band_backbones.tsv.

candidate_tracks._disabled_reason: 2026-05-19: pipeline does not currently emit candidate_tracks.json.

layers._section_3: ==== WARM cohort-level layers (loaded once at app start) ====
layers._succession_note_3: These layers are PROVISIONAL in inversion-atlas. They semantically belong to a future population-atlas. When that atlas lands and declares these same keys, the registry's succession rule lets population take over silently. See SPEC_registry_v1.md §7 and README_PAIRING.md §11.

cohort_relatedness._doc: Aggregated cohort relatedness JSON: {pairs: [{sample_a, sample_b, kinship, relationship_class, ...}], samples?, kinship_thresholds?, _provenance?}. Source of truth for mendelian.js / mendelian_inheritance.js / lineage inference. Distinct from `relatedness_ngsrelate` which is the raw per-tool TSV; this is the aggregator's output combining one or more tool runs. SPEC_v2 §4 replaced the empty placeholder schema with the real one in 2026-05-12. schema_status remains 'pending' until a real file lands at the path — flip to 'validated' to enable resolver-side validation.

layers._section_4_versioning_note: All per-candidate layers below template on BOTH {candidate_id} AND {version_id}. version_id is required at call time — there is no fallback default. The active version_id for a given candidate lives in candidate_lineage.active_version_id (the lineage layer below). Pages typically resolve lineage first, then resolve other per-candidate layers with that version_id.

candidate_lineage._doc: The version index for a candidate. Names all versions ever computed and which is active. Boundaries, K, locked_labels are NOT here — those live per-version under data/candidates/{candidate_id}/{version_id}/. lineage.json is the index, not the data. NOT version-scoped (one per candidate, regardless of how many versions). writable: true — browser refinement workflows append new version entries via Registry.write.

candidates_v1._doc: Cohort-level inversion candidate list. The session-persisted form of atlasState.inversion.candidateList. Each entry: { id, chrom, start_bp, end_bp, K, verdict, source, provisional, confirmed, locked_labels[], promoted_at }. Cross-atlas: read by evolution, popstats, cross-species, relatedness, meiosis, diversity, population. Promoted via catalogue/local_pca_dosage/haplotype_regimes pages. Added 2026-05-23 to back the cross_atlas.exports declaration.

regime_catalogue_v1._doc: Haplotype regime catalogue (Cluster 4 of the haplotype-regimes pipeline: regime_mendelian / regime_dyad_mendelian / regime_pedigree / regime_linkage). Per-regime classification + per-window membership. Cross-atlas: read by popstats (per-regime stats), relatedness (regime inheritance page), meiosis (long-range regime context). Added 2026-05-23 to back the cross_atlas.exports declaration.

candidate_gene_cargo._doc: version_id required. Gene cargo depends on boundaries, so each version has its own gene_cargo.

candidate_marker_primers._doc: version_id required. Primers are version-specific (different boundaries -> different breakpoint regions -> different primers).

candidate_breeding_card._doc: version_id required. Browser-side analysis output (per DATA_LIFECYCLE Category 3 browser-side producer).

layers._section_5: ==== COLD comparative layers (loaded only when a comparative page mounts) ====
layers._succession_note_5: Synteny + phylogeny are genome-level concepts. These layers will move to a future genome-atlas. te_fragility stays in inversion (it's specifically about TE-driven inversion-formation).

te_fragility._doc: STAYS in inversion-atlas — TE fragility specifically explains why inversions form, not a generic genome layer.

layers._section_6_audit: Operations match popstats_server.py routes verified 2026-05-06 against Atlas_turn166_round2_2026-05-05. The legacy registry had invented endpoints (fst_hom1_hom2, theta_pi_by_invgt etc.) that don't exist in the server. The real server has FOUR compute endpoints: popstats_groupwise (FST+dXY+theta_pi together), popstats_hobs_groupwise (HoverE), ancestry_groupwise_q, ld_split_heatmap. Plus dosage and shelf-LD.

fst_dxy_thetapi_groupwise._doc: Note: FST, dXY, theta_pi all come back from ONE call to popstats_groupwise — they're three metrics in the response, not three separate operations. The page picks which to display. Cache key includes the metric set so requesting only fst doesn't pollute a request for all three. persist: true — ANGSD over 226 samples is heavy; result is written to the server results cache and a re-call hits cached JSON instead of recomputing.

hobs_groupwise._doc: persist: true — hobs over the cohort at multiple scales is heavy; cache the result.

ancestry_q_groupwise._doc: persist: true — NGSadmix-equivalent groupwise Q is heavy.

ld_split_heatmap_layer._doc: persist: true — split-heatmap LD over a region is moderately heavy and re-asked frequently when comparing candidates.

shelf_ld_test_layer._doc: persist: true — small but called per-candidate; cache to avoid recompute on revisit.

dosage_chunk_layer._doc: Used by per-sample lines panel. Lazy-loaded on demand — the operation needs start/end bp args that the prewarm scheduler cannot supply from shared.activeChrom alone (was preload_on: candidate_change, but that fired without start/end and the server returned 422 Unprocessable Entity). Pages that need this layer resolve it explicitly with {chrom, start, end, cap}. 2026-05-26.

layers._dropped_layers_doc: REMOVED from this registry: lof_burden, pseudogenisation_scan, coverage_extract, beagle_uncertainty, split_read_aggregate, permutation_test. These were invented in the previous round; their endpoints do NOT exist in popstats_server.py. If any of these are needed in the future, the corresponding endpoint must be added to popstats_server.py first, THEN registered here. Don't add layer entries pointing at non-existent endpoints.

arrangement_calls._doc: Per SPEC_arrangement_color_mode_and_arrangement_calls_v1.md. Wire format defined there. Used by per-sample-lines panel as 9th color mode. version_id required — arrangement calls depend on which boundary version they were derived against.

layers._section_8: ==== Browser-side ANALYSIS results (computed on demand by analysis/*.js modules; cached at warm tier) ====

candidate_karyotype_per_sample._doc: Per-sample HOM_REF/HET/HOM_INV/AMBIGUOUS assignment derived from local PCA on dosage. Browser-side compute (k-means K=3 on PC1/PC2 across the candidate's slab + per-sample purity gate; sort-by-PC1 maps label 0/1/2 to HOM_REF/HET/HOM_INV). Cached because used by mendelian, by per-sample lines panel, by marker assay design. NOT the file-cached candidate_final_class — that's the manuscript-frozen version; this is the live per-session compute. 2026-05-26 RE-ENABLED — analysis module at atlases/inversion/analysis/karyotype_assignment.js is a shim re-exporting from atlases/popstats/analysis/karyotype_assignment.js.

mendelian_test._doc: Mendelian inheritance test for the candidate inversion across cohort trios. Inputs: candidate_karyotype_per_sample, cohort_relatedness. Browser-side; results cached so flipping pages doesn't recompute. The analysis module at atlases/inversion/analysis/mendelian.js is a shim that re-exports from atlases/popstats/analysis/mendelian.js (the canonical implementation co-located with mendelian_inheritance.js orchestrator). 2026-05-26 RE-ENABLED — _findTrios now implemented + tested. Disabled blocker: candidate_karyotype_per_sample (still TODO, see analysis/README.md). Once that lands this layer becomes resolvable end-to-end.

trio_inventory._doc: List of (father, mother, offspring) trios in the cohort, derived from cohort_relatedness. Cached once at startup; reused by mendelian, by linkage analysis, by inheritance-pattern visualizations. 2026-05-26 RE-ENABLED — analysis module at atlases/inversion/analysis/trio_finder.js is a shim re-exporting from atlases/popstats/analysis/trio_finder.js#findCohortTrios. Default threshold = '1st_degree' (permissive); pass ctx.relatedness_threshold='parent_offspring' for strict mode. See popstats/analysis/mendelian.js findTrios for the algorithm + known 3-gen limitation.

layers._doc_relatedness_block: ==== Relatedness domain (Mode B — raw folder interface) — see data/relatedness/README.md ====

relatedness_ngsrelate._doc: Per-pair ngsRelate output. Path templates on {run_id}. Default ngsRelate column set, see schema. The optional `fields:` filter (declared at layer level OR overridden per-call) lets analysis modules pull only needed columns. schema_status='pending' until a real run lands; flip to 'validated' then. Provisional/owned_by 'population' so the future population atlas can take over without conflict.

relatedness_samples_order._doc: Sidecar to the ngsRelate run. Single-column samples-in-order file. Used by analysis modules that need to map a/b indices back to canonical sample IDs.

layers._doc_ancestry_block: ==== Ancestry domain (Mode B static + operation-backed runtime) — see data/ancestry/README.md ====

ancestry_global_q._doc: Per-sample ancestry Q matrix from NGSadmix. Wired 2026-05-07 (post-step22) to use the registryAdapter export of shared/loaders/qopt_loader.js, which reads the headerless whitespace-separated .qopt + sidecar samples.txt and emits a self-describing ancestry_global_q_v1 artifact. The loader handles NGSadmix conventions (no header, mixed-whitespace separators, sample order from samples.txt). Default paths derived from {K} + optional {run_id}; callers can override via args.qopt_path / args.samples_path. This is the FIRST WORKED EXAMPLE of the activate-schema + extract-schema pattern (Quentin's design directive 2026-05-07): the activate-schema for this producer lives at registries/producers/load_ngsadmix_qopt.activate.json. A sibling producer (registries/data/operations.registry.json: ancestry_groupwise_q) emits the SAME extract-schema via a server-side run on a sample subset — conditional ancestry (band-1 vs band-2). Both are interchangeable downstream because they share the extract-schema. Replaces the prior file-source entry which was blocked on a 5-LOC parseDelimited extension; that extension landed alongside this wiring (hasHeader: false + 'whitespace' sentinel sep).

_legacy_v0._doc: Pre-2026-05-07 entry, kept for traceability. Was blocked on parseDelimited needing header=false support. Resolved by the loader pattern above.

ancestry_global_q_samples._doc: Sample-order sidecar for the global Q file. Reuses the relatedness samples-order schema (same shape: one column, sample_id).

ancestry_local_q_windows._doc: Long-format ancestry-by-window for one chrom. Pre-aggregated by the pipeline from instant_q outputs. 2026-05-20: switched preload_on from 'chrom_change' to 'explicit' — the path template needs both {chrom} AND {K}, but the prewarm scheduler only fills the canonical chrom/candidate_id/species aliases. The unresolved {K} placeholder threw a templateFill error on every chrom change. Pages that consume this layer must resolve it manually with a {chrom, K} args object.

layers._doc_cross_species_block: ==== Cross-species domain (Mode B raw + Mode A curated) — see data/cross_species/README.md ====

cross_species_synteny_blocks._doc: Aggregated synteny blocks for one genome pair. Pair convention: '<ref>__vs__<query>'. Owned by future genome atlas.

cross_species_breakpoint_reuse._doc: Shared/reused breakpoints between two genomes. Joined from synteny edges + SV evidence. Owned by future genome atlas.
